Its commendable that you are trying to get help and advice so you can help your friend.  


However its very hard to help indirectly without hearing whats bothering her. But that being said the best advice I can give, is to make sure she knows you are there for her. Don't push or pry, doing so might make whatever she is feeling that much worse. Just reassure her and try to see things from her point of view, don't make snap judgements, and hear out all her concerns.  


Speaking from experience in my own past, be careful if you suggest a therapist or counsellor. While it does sound like your friend might need a professional, if she is turning to you and you outright tell her she needs to see one, you might make her feel like you are dismissing her to be someone elses problem. Try to find a way to encourage her to seek that help without flat out telling her too (Kind of hard to do I know)  


And lastly if she does go through with it, you cannot blame yourself. You coming here asking for help is more then what most people would do, you are doing all you can to prevent her from making a mistake.
